title: Use clear language (writing to GOV.UK standards)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Split sentences over 25 words; no more than 5 sentences a paragraph; active voice; plain words; explain specialist terms; positive contractions such as "you'll" are fine; literacy figures for the four UK nations.

title: Plain language guide series
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Plain language as content the audience understands; the Plain Writing Act of 2010 requires public content written for its audience; adapts the archived PlainLanguage.gov content (plainlanguage.gov now redirects here).

title: Plain language: writing
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Active voice, present tense, avoid hidden verbs (nouns made from verbs).

title: How to write clearly
publisher: European Commission, Directorate-General for Translation (Publications Office of the EU)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. EU clear writing guide published 2011, available in the 24 official EU languages.

title: Voice qualities (tutorial: rate of speech)
publisher: National Center for Voice and Speech
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Average rate of speech for US English speakers is about 150 words per minute.

title: Rehearse your slide show with Speaker Coach
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Checks pacing, pitch, filler words, informal speech, euphemisms, culturally sensitive terms and reading slide text; platforms; English only; report disappears when closed.

title: Use Presenter View in PowerPoint
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Presenter view shows current and next slide, speaker notes, a timer and the time; notes text can be made larger.

title: Present slides (Google Slides)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Presenter view with speaker notes; audience Q&A; captions can be toggled while presenting, English only.

title: Present with real-time, automatic captions or subtitles in PowerPoint
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Live captions and translated subtitles in more than 60 languages; needs a fast connection; headset microphone advised; speech is sent to Microsoft.

title: Present slides with captions (Google Slides)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Captions in Chrome, Edge and Safari; no punctuation; not stored; only the speaker is captioned; accuracy varies with accent and intonation; ask the audience first.

title: Use live captions in Microsoft Teams meetings
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Any participant can turn on captions; translated captions need a Teams Premium or Microsoft Copilot licence; CART captions supported; Teams does not save captions.

title: Plan for Teams events
supports: Opened with WebFetch (updated 4 Nov 2026). Event sizes, Speaker Coach in events if the admin allows, AI captions only in large-audience events, translated caption languages, and the advice to always run a dry run.

title: Making Events Accessible: Checklist for meetings, conferences, training, and presentations
supports: Opened with WebFetch (updated 31 Aug 2022). Send slides early in adaptable formats; describe visuals; speak clearly and not too fast; repeat audience questions; brief captioners and interpreters early; CART defined.

title: Understanding Success Criterion 1.2.4: Captions (Live)
supports: Opened with WebFetch (updated 9 Mar 2026). Level AA; captions for live audio in synchronised media; aimed at broadcasts, not two-way calls.

title: ADA Requirements: Effective Communication
supports: Opened with WebFetch (updated 28 Feb 2020). Title II and III entities; auxiliary aids including CART, captioning and interpreters; primary consideration to the person's choice under Title II.

title: Accessible communication formats
supports: Opened with WebFetch (updated 17 Jun 2026). NRCPD-regulated BSL interpreters; captions; Easy Read lead times; large print of 16 point or above; formats available at the same time as the standard version.

title: A new era of inclusion begins: the European Accessibility Act enters into force
supports: Opened with WebFetch. EAA applies from 28 June 2025 to listed products and services; speeches and meetings are not named.

title: Writing a business plan
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Order: company purpose, problem, solution, why now, market potential, competition, business model, team, financials, vision.

title: Satya Nadella email to employees on first day as CEO
supports: Opened with WebFetch. 4 Feb 2014 message built on four questions: who am I, why am I here, why are we here, what do we do next.

title: More information on fair use
supports: Opened with WebFetch (Index updated Nov 2026). Four factors; decided case by case; no safe word count or percentage; not legal advice.

title: Exceptions to copyright
supports: Opened with WebFetch (updated 4 Jan 2021). Fair dealing for criticism, review or quotation, with sufficient acknowledgement; usually only part of a work.

title: Final Rule: Selective Disclosure and Insider Trading (Regulation FD)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Listed issuers must not disclose material nonpublic information selectively; unintentional disclosure must be made public promptly; effective 23 Oct 2000.

title: UK Market Abuse Regulation
supports: Opened with WebFetch (updated 23 Feb 2026). UK MAR bans unlawful disclosure of inside information and requires prompt disclosure by issuers; it is the UK version of EU MAR.

title: Social anxiety (social phobia)
supports: Opened with WebFetch (reviewed 17 May 2023; next review was due 17 May 2026). See a GP if social anxiety has a big impact; self-referral to NHS talking therapies is possible.
